name: ponytail
description: Makes your AI agent think like the laziest senior dev in the room. The best code is the code you never wrote.
readmeExcerpt:
Ponytail

He says nothing. He writes one line. It works.

~54% less code (up to 94%) · ~20% cheaper · ~27% faster · 100% safe
Real Claude Code sessions editing a real FastAPI + React repo, the same agent with and without the skill (12 feature tasks, Haiku 4.5, n=4). Details.

Español · 한국어 · 简体中文 · 日本語

---

## Already built with Ponytail --- You know him. Long ponytail. Oval glasses. Has been at the company longer than the version control. You show him fifty lines; he looks at them, says nothing, and replaces them with one. Ponytail puts him inside your AI agent. ## The prompt Ponytail is one prompt: [`skills/ponytail/SKILL.md`](skills/ponytail/SKILL.md). The compact version, for agents that read a rules file, is [`AGENTS.md`](AGENTS.md). Everything else in this repo loads that prompt into different agents. ## Install **Claude Code**, as two separate prompts: ``` /plugin marketplace add DietrichGebert/ponytail ``` ``` /plugin install ponytail@ponytail ``` **Codex:** ```bash codex plugin marketplace add DietrichGebert/ponytail codex plugin add ponytail@ponytail ``` Then open `/hooks` in Codex, trust its two lifecycle hooks, and start a new thread. **Any other agent:** copy [`AGENTS.md`](AGENTS.md) into your project, or ask your agent to install [`skills/ponytail/SKILL.md`](skills/ponytail/SKILL.md) as a skill. Step by step for Copilot, Cursor, OpenCode, Gemini and the rest: **[INSTALL.md](INSTALL.md)**. That was it. He'd be proud. He won't say it. Active every session, with a handful of commands (see [Commands](#commands)). `/ponytail ultra` exists for when the codebase has wronged you personally. Startup and mode-change text shows the current mode. Only install ponytail from `DietrichGebert/ponytail` on GitHub or `@dietrichgebert/ponytail` on npm. It never ships `.exe` or `.dll` files; a copy that does is not mine. ## Before / after You ask for a date picker. Your agent installs flatpickr, writes a wrapper component, adds a stylesheet, and starts a discussion about timezones. With ponytail: ```html ``` More survivors in [examples/](examples/). ## How it works Before writing code, the agent stops at the first rung that holds: ``` 1. Does this need to exist? → no: skip it (YAGNI) 2. Already in this codebase? → reuse it, don't rewrite 3. Stdlib does it? → use it 4. Native platform feature? → use it 5. Installed dependency? → use it 6. One line? → one line 7. Only then: the minimum that works ``` The ladder runs *after* it understands the problem, not instead of it: it reads the code the change touches and traces the real flow before picking a rung. Lazy about the solution, never about reading. Lazy, not negligent: trust-boundary validation, data-loss handling, security, and accessibility are never on the chopping block. ## Commands | Command | What it does | |---------|--------------| | `/ponytail [lite \| full \| ultra \| off]` | Set the intensity, or turn it off. No argument switches ponytail on at the default level if it is off, and otherwise reports the current level. | | `/ponytail-review` | Review the current diff for over-engineering, hands back a delete-list. Name a target in plain words to narrow or widen it: `uncommitted`, `staged`, `branch`, or a PR link. | | `/ponytail-audit` | Audit the whole repo for over-engineering, not just the diff. | | `/ponytail-debt` | Harvest the `ponytail:` shortcuts you've deferred into a ledger, so "later" doesn't become "never". | | `/ponytail-gain` | Show the measured impact scoreboard (less code, less cost, more speed) from the benchmark. | | `/ponytail-help` | Quick reference for the commands above. | Commands need a skill-capable host (Claude Code, Codex, Devin CLI, OpenCode, Gemini, pi, Hermes Agent, Qoder, Grok Build). In Codex CLI and the IDE extension they're skills under the plugin's namespace; invoke with `$ponytail:ponytail-review`. Cursor with the [hooks](INSTALL.md#cursor) gets `/ponytail` level switching only, typed as a plain message. The instruction-only adapters (Cursor's rule file, Windsurf, Cline, Copilot, Kiro, Antigravity) load the always-on ruleset without the commands. ## Numbers The honest measurement is a real agent doing real work: a headless Claude Code session editing [tiangolo's full-stack-fastapi-template](https://github.com/fastapi/full-stack-fastapi-template) (a real FastAPI + React repo), scored on the `git diff` it leaves behind. Twelve feature tickets, the same agent with and without the skill, n=4, Haiku 4.5.

| vs no-skill baseline | LOC | tokens | cost | time | safe | |---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:| | **ponytail** | **-54%** | **-22%** | **-20%** | **-27%** | **100%** | | caveman (terse-prose control) | -20% | +7% | +3% | +2% | 100% | | "YAGNI + one-liners" prompt | -33% | -14% | -21% | -30% | 95% | ponytail is the only arm that cuts every metric, and the only one that stays fully safe while doing it. The cut is biggest where there is a real over-build trap (date picker 404 to 23 lines, color picker 287 to 23, because it reaches for a native `` instead of a component) and near zero on code that is already minimal. Full method, per-task tables, and limitations: [benchmarks/results/2026-06-18-agentic.md](benchmarks/results/2026-06-18-agentic.md).
Older single-shot numbers (isolated generation) Five everyday tasks, three models, three arms (no skill, [caveman](https://github.com/JuliusBrussee/caveman), ponytail), ten runs, median reported. One prompt, one completion, counting lines of the answer:

This showed **80-94% less code**. [#126](https://github.com/DietrichGebert/ponytail/issues/126) fairly pointed out that the bare-model baseline pads its answer with prose and options, so that gap is partly a conversational-baseline artifact. The agentic numbers above are the corrected, defensible version. Reproduce the single-shot run with `npx promptfoo eval -c benchmarks/promptfooconfig.yaml`.
**The rule was never "fewest tokens."** It is: write only what the task needs, and never cut validation, error handling, security, or accessibility. The code ends up small because it is necessary, not golfed. Lower cost and latency are a side effect on the models that follow the ladder; a terse reasoning model that spends thinking tokens deliberating the rungs can go the other way (on GPT-5.5 it does). ## FAQ **Can I use it with [caveman](https://github.com/JuliusBrussee/caveman)?** Yes, and you should. Caveman shrinks what the agent says; ponytail shrinks what it builds. Different halves, no overlap: caveman leaves code byte-for-byte exact, ponytail stays out of the prose. Terse talk about minimal code. **Does it need a config file?** No. An optional `~/.config/ponytail/config.json` or `PONYTAIL_DEFAULT_MODE` env var can set the default level, but nothing is required. **What if I really need the 120-line cache class?** You don't. Insist anyway and he'll build it. Slowly. Correctly. While looking at you. **Does it scale?** The code you never wrote scales infinitely. Zero bugs, zero CVEs, 100% uptime since forever. **Why "ponytail"?** You know exactly why. ## Sponsors

releases.name: v4.13.0
releases.body:
This release is mostly about ponytail staying at the level you set. Switching levels on Codex now delivers the new level's rules, each project keeps its own mode, off really means off, and the statusline badge survives plugin updates. Kimi Code joins as a new host, the README now also comes in Spanish, Korean, Simplified Chinese and Japanese, and ZCode support is dropped.

## What's Changed
* fix(hooks): preserve mode on invalid arguments by @l2yujw in https://github.com/DietrichGebert/ponytail/pull/677
* fix(hooks): don't emit a second JSON object on Qoder report-only /pon… by @adiraj66132 in https://github.com/DietrichGebert/ponytail/pull/617
* fix(qoder): persist off mode across prompts by @l2yujw in https://github.com/DietrichGebert/ponytail/pull/676
* fix(hooks): silence off-mode SessionStart by @connerohnesorge in https://github.com/DietrichGebert/ponytail/pull/687
* Normalize default-mode parsing and add regression test by @thb-hash in https://github.com/DietrichGebert/ponytail/pull/716
* Fix Codex Ponytail mode instructions by @nainbaloch in https://github.com/DietrichGebert/ponytail/pull/932
* docs: use the namespaced $ponytail:<skill> form for Codex by @DietrichGebert in

releases.name: v4.12.0
releases.body:
Review and audit findings are numbered now, so you can answer "fix 2 and 4" instead of quoting lines back. CodeBuddy runs ponytail through the existing Claude plugin, and `/ponytail-gain` shows the honest agentic benchmark averages (54% less code, 22% fewer tokens, 20% lower cost, 27% faster, safety kept) instead of the old single-shot numbers a chatty baseline inflated. The README got slimmer too: every per-agent install step now lives in INSTALL.md.

## What's Changed
* docs: add Qwen Code support by @Dattuog in https://github.com/DietrichGebert/ponytail/pull/888
* feat: CodeBuddy support via the existing Claude plugin (#854) by @ShantanuTaro in https://github.com/DietrichGebert/ponytail/pull/891
* feat: add Goose adapter docs and schema guard (#880) by @nolanchic in https://github.com/DietrichGebert/ponytail/pull/882
* docs: add Muse Code CLI support by @dangtrungan in https://github.com/DietrichGebert/ponytail/pull/950
* docs: note that /ponytail-review takes a target in plain words by @DietrichGebert in https://github.com/DietrichGebert/ponytail/pull/1023
* feat: number review and audit findings (#327) by @yashrao2607 in https://github.com/DietrichGebert/ponytail/pull/523
* do

releases.name: v4.11.0
releases.body:
If you use ponytail in Codex, update. Since v4.10.2 a one-line change in the root `plugin.json` made Codex, VS Code and Qwen load ponytail as a skills-only Agent Plugin, so the hooks never registered and the rules never reached the model. This release takes that line out and they get the full ponytail again. On top of that, Hermes sends the ruleset once instead of every turn, review and audit learn a `reuse` tag, and seven more agents get documented setups.

## What's Changed
* docs: fix Codex skill invocation syntax by @dangtrungan in https://github.com/DietrichGebert/ponytail/pull/951
* fix(debt): catch /* ponytail: */ block comments and skip .git, node_modules, dist, build in the scan by @DEOWL-kan in https://github.com/DietrichGebert/ponytail/pull/815
* fix(audit): require a whole-tree caller check before delete: (#679) by @szsunyuan in https://github.com/DietrichGebert/ponytail/pull/714
* feat: add reuse tag to ponytail-review and ponytail-audit (#868) by @nolanchic in https://github.com/DietrichGebert/ponytail/pull/881
* fix(skills): drop the duplicate reuse tag line in review and audit by @DietrichGebert in https://github.com/DietrichGebert/ponytail/pull/984
* fix(hermes): a

releases.name: v4.10.3
releases.body:
Several sessions, one machine, no more fighting. The ponytail mode is now kept per project, so a session in one repo no longer switches or clears the mode of a session in another. A bare `/ponytail` behaves the same everywhere (off switches on, on just reports the level), ZCode finally gets the ruleset, and Codex stops showing a yellow warning at every start.

## What's Changed
* fix(hooks): do not persist review from /ponytail-review (#736) by @szsunyuan in https://github.com/DietrichGebert/ponytail/pull/750
* fix(hooks): keep the live mode per project so concurrent sessions stop overwriting each other by @DietrichGebert in https://github.com/DietrichGebert/ponytail/pull/981
* fix(codex): drop SessionStart systemMessage that renders as a yellow warning (#605) by @spde in https://github.com/DietrichGebert/ponytail/pull/606
* fix: emit hookSpecificOutput JSON on ZCode so rules reach the model by @Arteiimis in https://github.com/DietrichGebert/ponytail/pull/799
* fix: read ponytail MCP package version by @ousamabenyounes in https://github.com/DietrichGebert/ponytail/pull/587
* fix: bare /ponytail switches ponytail on, or reports the level when it already is by @DietrichGebert in http

releases.name: v4.10.2
releases.body:
A security and reliability release. The lifecycle hooks no longer splice the plugin path into shell text, a slow subagent matcher can no longer hang a session, and npm publishing now waits for green tests. On top of that, Windows and WSL hooks stop hanging and find their scripts again, Pi keeps its prompt cache, OMP keeps its prompt parts, and Hermes installs work again. Thanks to the eleven first-time contributors in this one.

## What's Changed
* fix: harden OIDC publishing dependencies and test gate by @Inference1 in https://github.com/DietrichGebert/ponytail/pull/831
* fix(pi): inject via systemPromptOptions.sections to preserve prompt cache by @HoneyTyagii in https://github.com/DietrichGebert/ponytail/pull/963
* fix(pi): keep before_agent_start systemPrompt as array for OMP by @aniruddhaadak80 in https://github.com/DietrichGebert/ponytail/pull/780
* fix: reword benchmark doc lines that force DANGEROUS plugin-scan verdict by @harshil-darji in https://github.com/DietrichGebert/ponytail/pull/826
* chore: declare agent-plugins.org 1.0.0 manifest in root plugin.json by @shashikanth171 in https://github.com/DietrichGebert/ponytail/pull/744
* fix: require a quoted value for Hermes mo

/plugin marketplace add DietrichGebert/ponytail

Before / after

You ask for a date picker. Your agent installs flatpickr, writes a wrapper component, adds a stylesheet, and starts a discussion about timezones.

With ponytail:

<!-- ponytail: browser has one -->
<input type="date">

How it works

Before writing code, the agent stops at the first rung that holds:

1. Does this need to exist?   → no: skip it (YAGNI)
2. Already in this codebase?  → reuse it, don't rewrite
3. Stdlib does it?            → use it
4. Native platform feature?   → use it
5. Installed dependency?      → use it
6. One line?                  → one line
7. Only then: the minimum that works

The ladder runs after it understands the problem, not instead of it: it reads the code the change touches and traces the real flow before picking a rung. Lazy about the solution, never about reading.

Lazy, not negligent: trust-boundary validation, data-loss handling, security, and accessibility are never on the chopping block.

Command What it does

/ponytail-audit Audit the whole repo for over-engineering, not just the diff.

/ponytail-gain Show the measured impact scoreboard (less code, less cost, more speed) from the benchmark.
/ponytail-help Quick reference for the commands above.

Commands need a skill-capable host (Claude Code, Codex, Devin CLI, OpenCode, Gemini, pi, Hermes Agent, Qoder, Grok Build). In Codex CLI and the IDE extension they're skills under the plugin's namespace; invoke with $ponytail:ponytail-review. Can I use it with caveman? Yes, and you should. Caveman shrinks what the agent says; ponytail shrinks what it builds. Different halves, no overlap: caveman leaves code byte-for-byte exact, ponytail stays out of the prose. Terse talk about minimal code.

aiSummary.oneLiner: An AI agent skill that enforces minimal, safe, and dependency-free one-liner code generation.
aiSummary.whatItDoes: Ponytail operates as an always-on ruleset for AI coding agents to drastically reduce code generation bloat and avoid unnecessary complexities. It forces the agent to read existing codebase context and standard libraries before writing, ensuring it reuses existing implementations rather than hallucinating new dependencies. The system applies a strict decision ladder that prioritizes dropping unnecessary tasks, reusing native platform capabilities, and writing the absolute minimum required code without sacrificing security or accessibility. By integrating directly into agents like Claude Code and Copilot via lifecycle hooks, it reduces token usage, latency, and costs significantly across tasks.
keyFeatures: Decision ladder enforcement: Stops agents from over-building by sequentially verifying if a feature can be skipped, reused, or solved natively.
Contextual awareness: Forces the agent to trace real codebase flow and read modified areas before outputting any code.
Safety preservation: Ensures trust-boundary validation, error handling, and accessibility are never compromised during minimization.
Universal agent injection: Integrates seamlessly via lifecycle hooks into popular AI platforms like Claude Code, Codex, Copilot CLI, and Gemini.
Cost and token reduction: Measurably decreases generation tokens and operational costs by preventing agents from writing boilerplate wrappers.

useCases.description: Teams operating headless AI agents can cut API costs and token usage by enforcing minimal, non-verbose code modifications.

useCases.title: Standard Library Prioritization
useCases.description: Engineers can force their AI assistants to utilize built-in standard libraries instead of unnecessarily pulling in external npm packages.

useCases.title: Secure Code Minimization
useCases.description: Developers can safely shrink codebases knowing the AI is instructed to retain all critical data-loss handling and trust-boundary validations.

aiSummary.whoIsItFor: Ponytail is for developers heavily utilizing AI coding assistants who are frustrated by bloated, overly complex code generation. It is designed for engineers seeking lean, maintainable, and cost-efficient agentic workflows.
